verdict.headline: AI infrastructure names rally on CoreWeave Q2 beat as Brent hits new high ahead of CPI
verdict.label: 3-of-6 regime active: CRWV +16% pre-market on Q2 beat; NVDA $222; Brent $91.60 (sixth advance); July CPI 8:30 AM ET
verdict.rationale_short: CoreWeave's clean Q2 — $104B backlog, Meta $21B + Anthropic + Jane Street diversifying the customer book — drove CRWV +16% pre-market and NVDA to $222.05, with Apollo, BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, and KKR committing to mobilize $500B+ in AI infrastructure capital. Against that AI-demand positive, Brent added $3.37 overnight to $91.60, the sixth consecutive advance on Hormuz skepticism — a level that increases the energy comp's contribution to July CPI's 3.4% YoY consensus due 8:30 AM ET. The level that changes the equity-resilience read: SPX closes below 7,600 on or within two sessions of the print.

trade_setups.asset: July CPI — Wednesday August 12, 8:30 AM ET
trade_setups.thesis: CPI arrives with a split setup: CRWV's $104B backlog is the AI-demand anchor in pre-market; Brent at $91.60 is the energy-comp escalation since Tuesday's close. July CPI embeds Brent at $82-92/bbl from the June-July peak; the overnight $91.60 is a floor, not a tailwind. Kalshi pricing less than 55% above 3.3% reflects Tuesday's small-cap rate-sensitivity positioning — not the overnight Brent move. Below 2.9%/3.2%: 30Y compresses, oil treated transient, September below 25%, CRWV/NVDA pre-market gains compound. Ambiguous (2.9-3.2%/3.2-3.5%): 30Y holds, Jackson Hole August 27 decides. Hot (≥3.2%/3.5%): supply-shock channel confirmed with labor already negative; 30Y toward 5.30%+; pre-market AI bid partially unwound.
trade_setups.entry: Watch 30Y direction in the first 30 minutes post-print: below 5.10% is the first de-escalation signal; above 5.28% is the hot-print entrenchment signal.
trade_setups.invalidation: Soft print (below 2.9%/3.2%) removes September hike as near-term narrative and resets odds below 25%.
trade_setups.horizon: 8:30 AM ET today; secondary read Thursday and Friday.

trade_setups.asset: Brent Crude — above $90 with SPCX tranche and Jackson Hole ahead
trade_setups.thesis: Brent at $91.60 is the sixth consecutive advance on Iran PGSA governance with no Hormuz deal in sight — Iran's Zolghadr conditions unchanged, Pakistan's deal claim disputed by Tehran, Houthi strikes on Red Sea alternatives continuing. Each prior deal-failure sequence was followed by an oil recovery from a temporary dip; the $91.60 level before CPI is structurally different from a temporary spike. If CPI embeds the energy comp and the 30Y holds above 5.22%, the SPCX August 20 tranche supply gate arrives with both an oil headwind and rate pressure simultaneously.
trade_setups.entry: Brent $91.60 (above $85 trigger). WTI ~$84 (above $79 trigger). Both regime triggers active.
trade_setups.invalidation: Brent closes below $87 on two consecutive sessions, signaling Oman channel progress.
trade_setups.horizon: Through August 20 SPCX tranche and August 27 Jackson Hole keynote.

bear_case: The CRWV positive resolves the AI-demand binary but leaves three macro conditions active, and the overnight oil escalation has made the picture worse, not better. Brent at $91.60 pre-CPI is $3.37 above Tuesday's close and $6.60 above the $85 formal trigger — the highest level since the early July Hormuz crisis peak. Iran's Zolghadr conditions are unchanged, Pakistan's deal optimism was disputed by Tehran, and Houthi strikes on Red Sea shipping alternatives continued overnight. July CPI embeds Brent at $82-92/bbl from the June-July peak; if the 3.4% YoY consensus prints at or above 3.5% headline, Kashkari's supply-shock framework is confirmed with labor already negative from the July NFP (-23K). The 30Y at 5.22% has been above 5.00% for twelve sessions; a hot CPI print sends the next reference level to 5.30%, compressing the multiple on AI infrastructure names whose pre-market gains price the benign scenario. The level that changes the equity-resilience read: SPX closes below 7,600 within two sessions of today's print.
